key_insight: The paper proposes a smooth, explicit elastoplastic-damage material update that preserves history dependence and irreversibility without solving a local Newton problem.
engineering_relevance: It offers a compact and vectorizable constitutive update for graphics simulation, making plastically deforming and degrading solids easier to implement in explicit solvers.
method: Softplus generates a candidate equivalent plastic strain, then a max-history projection enforces irreversibility.
A deviatoric plastic-strain tensor stores residual direction while an exponential damage variable evolves from the same history.
Active and frozen branches are evaluated analytically from one response energy, avoiding local root-finding.
evidence_signal: Across 1D, 2D, and 3D tests, the method reproduced residual deformation and monotone internal variables, but a 90-degree loading turn produced a 49.39% normalized equivalent-stress error versus 1.53% under proportional loading.
watch_item: The approach is intended for isotropic, proportional or near-proportional loading; it is not suitable as a general replacement for return mapping or anisotropic damage models.
paper_title: A Smooth Explicit Elastoplastic--Damage Update for Graphics Simulation
